native.command:
set -eu
agentmgr_zcode_source="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentmgr/zcode"
if [ -e "$HOME/.local/bin/zcode" ] || [ -L "$HOME/.local/bin/zcode" ]; then
  printf "%s\n" "zcode already exists in ~/.local/bin; use its existing installation to update" >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$agentmgr_zcode_source")" "$HOME/.local/bin"
if [ -d "$agentmgr_zcode_source/.git" ]; then
  test "$(git -C "$agentmgr_zcode_source" remote get-url origin)" = "https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode.git"
  git -C "$agentmgr_zcode_source" pull --ff-only
else
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/zai-org/ZCode.git "$agentmgr_zcode_source"
fi
cd "$agentmgr_zcode_source"
pnpm bootstrap
pnpm --filter @zcode/cli... build
chmod u+x "$agentmgr_zcode_source/apps/zcode-cli/packages/cli/dist/zcode.cjs"
node "$agentmgr_zcode_source/apps/zcode-cli/packages/cli/dist/zcode.cjs" --version
ln -s "$agentmgr_zcode_source/apps/zcode-cli/packages/cli/dist/zcode.cjs" "$HOME/.local/bin/zcode"
native.update_cmd:
set -eu
agentmgr_zcode_source="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentmgr/zcode"
cd "$agentmgr_zcode_source"
git pull --ff-only
pnpm bootstrap
pnpm --filter @zcode/cli... build
chmod u+x "$agentmgr_zcode_source/apps/zcode-cli/packages/cli/dist/zcode.cjs"
node "$agentmgr_zcode_source/apps/zcode-cli/packages/cli/dist/zcode.cjs" --version

agentmgr_symphony_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$agentmgr_symphony_tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
cd "$agentmgr_symphony_tmp"
curl -fsSLo "$agentmgr_symphony_asset" "https://github.com/openai/symphony/releases/download/$agentmgr_symphony_tag/$agentmgr_symphony_asset"
curl -fsSLo "$agentmgr_symphony_asset.sha256" "https://github.com/openai/symphony/releases/download/$agentmgr_symphony_tag/$agentmgr_symphony_asset.sha256"
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sha256sum -c "$agentmgr_symphony_asset.sha256"
else
  shasum -a 256 -c "$agentmgr_symphony_asset.sha256"
fi
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
test ! -L "$HOME/.local/bin/symphony"
install -m 0755 "$agentmgr_symphony_asset" "$HOME/.local/bin/symphony"

metadata.install_note: Engineering preview. Installs a stable self-contained Unix release with checksum verification. Supply a configured WORKFLOW.md and tracker credentials separately; no version probe is run.

open-scion.name: open_scion
open-scion.description: Experimental community source-control system for coding agents with the Graft CLI

native.command:
set -eu
agentmgr_open_scion_source="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentmgr/open-scion"
if [ -e "$HOME/.local/bin/graft" ] || [ -L "$HOME/.local/bin/graft" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'graft already exists in ~/.local/bin; use its existing installation to update' >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$agentmgr_open_scion_source")" "$HOME/.local/bin"
if [ -d "$agentmgr_open_scion_source/.git" ]; then
  test "$(git -C "$agentmgr_open_scion_source" remote get-url origin)" = "https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git"
  git -C "$agentmgr_open_scion_source" pull --ff-only
else
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git "$agentmgr_open_scion_source"
fi
cd "$agentmgr_open_scion_source"
make build
test -x "$agentmgr_open_scion_source/_build/bin/graft"
ln -s "$agentmgr_open_scion_source/_build/bin/graft" "$HOME/.local/bin/graft"
native.update_cmd:
set -eu
agentmgr_open_scion_source="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentmgr/open-scion"
test "$(git -C "$agentmgr_open_scion_source" remote get-url origin)" = "https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git"
cd "$agentmgr_open_scion_source"
git pull --ff-only
make build

Requires Bash 3.2+, Git and OpenCode for agent workflows; Windows needs Git Bash or WSL. Installing the wrapper does not install agent patterns or configure a project; run OAC setup/install explicitly.

mcp-scanner.name: Cisco MCP Scanner
mcp-scanner.description: Analyzes MCP tool definitions and server code with configurable security scanners

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.11.4+; upstream selects Python 3.13. Set UV_PYTHON=3.13 when installing to select that interpreter. YARA and other native dependencies may need platform build tools. Choose scan targets/engines explicitly; live-server scans can execute server commands or contact services. Hosted/LLM analysis and VirusTotal need separate credentials.

mcp-filesystem.name: MCP Filesystem Server
mcp-filesystem.description: Provides configured local filesystem tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Uses the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem package and mcp-server-filesystem executable. Use a current Node runtime for SDK dependencies. Configure MCP clients and explicitly choose allowed directories before starting the server; filesystem access is limited by that configuration. Installation does not register or start an MCP server.

pydantic-clai.name: Pydantic AI CLI
pydantic-clai.description: Runs Pydantic AI agents and terminal conversations through the clai client

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.11+. Installs the official clai distribution, which includes the pydantic-ai dependency, rather than relying on the pai compatibility alias. This catalog method targets macOS/Linux terminal platforms. Configure model providers and choose custom agents or tools explicitly.

hayhooks.name: Hayhooks
hayhooks.description: Deploys Haystack agent and retrieval pipelines as HTTP and MCP endpoints

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. The hayhooks distribution supplies its CLI. Define pipeline wrappers and install pipeline-specific dependencies in the chosen environment separately. Deployment, server startup, MCP exposure and provider credentials are explicit setup steps.

mlx-lm.name: MLX LM
mlx-lm.description: Runs local language models and OpenAI-compatible inference for Apple silicon agents

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.11+ and Apple silicon macOS 14+ with a compatible MLX/Metal backend. This entry uses the base macOS distribution; Linux CPU/CUDA extras are not installed. Select models and explicitly download, chat, fine-tune or start mlx_lm.server separately; memory requirements depend on the model.

phoenix.name: Arize Phoenix CLI
phoenix.description: Serves tracing, inspection and evaluation tools for agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.11 through 3.14. The arize-phoenix package supplies phoenix and arize-phoenix. Start the local service explicitly; configure storage, tracing exporters, instrumentation, authentication and evaluation providers separately. Application instrumentation can send trace content to the configured endpoint.

langflow.name: Langflow CLI
langflow.description: Builds, runs and serves visual agent workflows and MCP-enabled flows

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. Langflow is a metapackage; expose the langflow-base dependency executable with uv --with-executables-from langflow-base while retaining langflow for inventory, upgrades and removal. Older AgentManager binaries must be upgraded/rebuilt for this metadata support. Start the service and configure flow dependencies, providers, storage and authentication explicitly.

apify-cli.name: Apify CLI
apify-cli.description: Develops and runs web-extraction Actors that provide data and tools to agents

metadata.notes: The CLI declares Node 20+, but its which 7 dependency requires Node 22.22.2+ on 22.x, 24.15+ on 24.x, or 26+. Use a compatible current runtime. Uses apify-cli rather than an Apify SDK; it also installs actor and apify-cli aliases. Create projects and authenticate explicitly. Local runs need their project/browser dependencies; cloud Actor runs or deployments can consume account resources.

magentic-ui.name: Magentic UI CLI
magentic-ui.description: Launches a human-supervised computer-use agent interface and backend

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.12+. The current upstream MagenticLite release tests macOS arm64 and Windows x64 through WSL2; native Linux x64 is expected but untested upstream. This catalog method supports macOS/Linux, with Windows users running inside WSL. Quicksand VM setup, Linux KVM access, model credentials and service startup are separate requirements.

marvin.name: Marvin CLI
marvin.description: Extracts and transforms structured data through agentic language-model workflows

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The marvin package supplies the CLI, including stdin extraction via marvin x and configuration/database commands. Configure model providers and storage explicitly. Model-backed operations can send selected input to the configured provider; installation does not execute a workflow.

llama-swap.name: llama-swap
llama-swap.description: Routes agent model requests and swaps local inference-server processes

metadata.notes: Uses the upstream Homebrew tap with x64/arm64 macOS/Linux binaries. Install inference backends, choose models and prepare a configuration separately. Starting the proxy can launch configured model-server commands; installation does not start it or download models.

bentoml.name: BentoML CLI
bentoml.description: Packages and serves model inference APIs used by agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.9+. The bentoml distribution supplies its CLI; model/framework dependencies belong in the selected service environment. Define services and configure models explicitly. Container builds need Docker, and cloud deployment needs separate account/authentication setup; installation does not deploy a service.

chroma.name: Chroma CLI
chroma.description: Runs and manages vector retrieval storage for agent memory and RAG workflows

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.9+. The chromadb distribution supplies chroma. Published native wheels cover macOS x64 10.12+/arm64 11+, glibc 2.17+ Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64; dependency requirements can be stricter. Choose storage and explicitly start a server or connect to cloud resources. Collection creation, embedding downloads and data ingestion are separate steps.

n8n.name: n8n CLI
n8n.description: Runs automation workflows that integrate agents, model calls and external tools

metadata.notes: Requires Node 24+. The npm n8n package includes the self-hosted workflow CLI/server, not a desktop app. Configure storage, encryption/authentication, credentials and workflow activation separately. Starting or executing workflows can call external services; installation does not start the service or activate workflows.

chrome-devtools-mcp.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
chrome-devtools-mcp.description: Gives coding agents Chrome inspection, debugging and browser automation tools

metadata.notes: Requires Node 20.19+ on 20.x, 22.12+ on 22.x, or 23+. Install a supported Chrome/Chrome for Testing browser and configure the MCP client separately. Upstream usage statistics are enabled by default; use --no-usage-statistics when starting the server to opt out. Installation does not start a browser or register the server.

tavily-mcp.name: Tavily MCP
tavily-mcp.description: Provides web search, extraction, crawling and research tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Upstream recommends Node 20+; use a current Node LTS runtime. Configure a Tavily API key, tool selection and MCP client separately. Search, crawl and research requests can consume account credits; installation does not start the server or send requests.

exa-mcp.name: Exa MCP Server
exa-mcp.description: Provides web and code search plus research tools for agent context

metadata.notes: Requires Node 20+. Configure Exa credentials, enabled tools and the MCP client separately. Service-backed search and research requests can consume account credits; installation does not start a server or submit searches.

firecrawl-mcp.name: Firecrawl MCP Server
firecrawl-mcp.description: Exposes website scraping, crawling and browser tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22+. This firecrawl-mcp package is separate from firecrawl-cli. Configure a Firecrawl API key or supported self-hosted endpoint and the MCP client separately. Crawls and browser operations can consume service resources; installation does not start the server or a crawl.

brave-search-mcp.name: Brave Search MCP
brave-search-mcp.description: Provides Brave web, image, news and local search tools for agents

metadata.notes: Use a current Node LTS runtime; the published commander dependency requires Node 20+. Configure a Brave Search API key, account access and MCP client separately. Installation does not start the server or perform searches.

perplexity-mcp.name: Perplexity MCP
perplexity-mcp.description: Connects agents to Perplexity search, reasoning and research tools

metadata.notes: Requires Node 18+; use a current Node LTS runtime. Configure a Perplexity API key, enabled tools and MCP client separately. Model and research requests can consume account credits; installation does not start a server or send prompts.

playwright-test.name: Playwright Test CLI
playwright-test.description: Runs browser tests and captures traces for coding-agent verification

metadata.notes: Requires Node 20+. The @playwright/test distribution supplies playwright and is distinct from playwright-cli and playwright-mcp. Browser downloads, Linux system dependencies and project test configuration are explicit setup steps. Installation does not run tests or install browsers.

huggingface-cli.name: Hugging Face CLI
huggingface-cli.description: Manages model and dataset artifacts used by agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The huggingface-hub distribution supplies hf and also publishes the tiny-agents executable. Configure login and access to gated repositories separately. Model/dataset downloads, uploads and agent/model-provider setup are explicit operations; installation does not download models.

github-mcp.name: GitHub MCP Server
github-mcp.description: Connects agents to scoped GitHub repository, issue and pull-request tools

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew CLI formula, separate from the hosted remote MCP endpoint. Configure GitHub authentication, token permissions, toolsets, read-only settings and the MCP client explicitly. Enabled tools can modify GitHub resources; installation does not connect or write to repositories.

aws-documentation-mcp.name: AWS Documentation MCP
aws-documentation-mcp.description: Retrieves and searches AWS documentation for agent infrastructure workflows

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The official distribution and executable use awslabs.aws-documentation-mcp-server; the catalog package uses its normalized hyphenated name so uv inventory, upgrades and removal match. Choose the documentation region/partition and MCP client configuration separately. This entry is the documentation server, not the other AWS MCP servers.

redis-mcp.name: Redis MCP Server
redis-mcp.description: Provides Redis data and command tools to configured agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: The published distribution requires Python 3.10+; follow upstream runtime guidance. Configure the Redis endpoint, authentication, ACLs, enabled commands and MCP client separately. Enabled tools can read or mutate Redis data; installation does not start Redis or connect to a database.

qdrant-mcp.name: Qdrant MCP Server
qdrant-mcp.description: Stores and retrieves semantic context for agents using Qdrant collections

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and a supported native embedding runtime. Configure a Qdrant endpoint or local storage, collection, embedding model and MCP client explicitly. First embedding use can download a model; data ingestion and server startup are separate steps. Native dependency support varies by OS and architecture.

mongodb-mcp.name: MongoDB MCP Server
mongodb-mcp.description: Provides database inspection, query and Atlas tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Requires Node 20.19+ on 20.x, 22.13+ on 22.x, or 24+. Configure a MongoDB connection or Atlas account, permissions, read-only/tool settings and MCP client separately. Optional native authentication or local Atlas features may need platform dependencies. Installation does not connect or modify databases.

dbhub.name: DBHub
dbhub.description: Provides configured multi-database SQL and schema tools to agents

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22.5+. Use @bytebase/dbhub, not the unrelated unscoped dbhub package. Configure database drivers, connections, permissions, read-only settings and MCP client explicitly; optional native drivers/SSH can need build tools. Installation does not connect to databases or run SQL.

supabase-mcp.name: Supabase MCP Server
supabase-mcp.description: Connects agents to scoped Supabase project and database tools

metadata.notes: Use a current Node LTS runtime; the published MCP Node dependency requires Node 20+. The canonical upstream repository is supabase/mcp. Configure authentication, project scope, read-only mode, toolsets and MCP client separately. Enabled tools can modify project resources; installation does not create or access projects.

kubernetes-mcp.name: Kubernetes MCP Server
kubernetes-mcp.description: Provides Kubernetes and OpenShift cluster tools for agent workflows

metadata.notes: Uses a Node wrapper with native optional packages for macOS/Linux/Windows x64 and arm64. Use a current Node LTS runtime and retain npm optional dependencies. Configure kubeconfig, context, permissions, read-only/tool settings and MCP client explicitly. Enabled tools can modify clusters; installation does not start or connect to a cluster.

terraform-mcp.name: Terraform MCP Server
terraform-mcp.description: Provides Terraform Registry and HCP Terraform context and tools to agents

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew CLI formula. Configure the MCP client, enabled toolsets and any HCP Terraform credentials/permissions separately. Service-backed operations use the selected account scope; installation does not start the server or perform Terraform/HCP operations.

azure-mcp.name: Azure MCP Server
azure-mcp.description: Connects agent MCP clients to configured Azure service tools

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22+. The npm wrapper loads native optional packages for macOS/Linux/Windows x64 and arm64; retain optional dependencies and meet upstream OS library requirements. Configure Azure authentication, subscriptions, permissions, toolsets and read-only settings explicitly. Installation does not sign in, provision resources or start the server.

neon-mcp.name: Neon MCP Server
neon-mcp.description: Provides Neon database, branch and project tools for agent workflows

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22+. Configure Neon credentials, project scope, permissions, read-only/tool selection and MCP client separately. Enabled tools can create branches, execute queries or modify resources; installation does not access or provision databases.

grafana-mcp.name: Grafana MCP Server
grafana-mcp.description: Gives agents configured Grafana observability and dashboard tools

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew CLI formula. Configure the Grafana URL, service-account token, permissions, datasource/tool selection and MCP client explicitly. Enabled tools can query telemetry or modify dashboards/resources; installation does not connect or start the server.

mcp-toolbox.name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
mcp-toolbox.description: Connects agents to configured databases using reusable MCP toolsets

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew formula and toolbox executable; it conflicts with other toolbox binaries such as KaHIP. Configure database sources, credentials, permissions, toolsets and the MCP client separately. Choose prebuilt tools or a tools configuration explicitly. Installation does not connect to databases or start the server.

mcp-atlassian.name: MCP Atlassian
mcp-atlassian.description: Provides Jira and Confluence project context and tools to agent clients

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. This is the community sooperset server, distinct from Atlassian hosted remote MCP. Configure Jira/Confluence endpoints, authentication, permissions, read-only/tool settings and MCP client separately. Enabled tools can modify issues or pages; installation does not connect to a workspace.

clickhouse-mcp.name: ClickHouse MCP Server
clickhouse-mcp.description: Provides ClickHouse query and analytics tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. This method installs the base ClickHouse server integration; embedded chDB needs the separate chdb extra. Configure endpoints, credentials, database access and MCP client explicitly. Query execution and server startup are separate operations.

motherduck-mcp.name: MotherDuck and DuckDB MCP
motherduck-mcp.description: Provides agent tools for local DuckDB data and MotherDuck analytics

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible DuckDB native wheels. Choose a local database path or MotherDuck endpoint/token and configure the MCP client separately. File connections are read-only by default; enabling writes or database switching is explicit. Installation does not create or open a database.

neo4j-mcp.name: Neo4j MCP Server
neo4j-mcp.description: Provides graph schema discovery and Cypher tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Uses the official macOS/Linux Homebrew CLI formula. Current bottles cover Apple silicon macOS and x64/arm64 Linux; other supported Homebrew hosts may need a Go source build. Configure the Neo4j URI, authentication, database, read-only mode, telemetry preference and MCP client separately. Installation does not start Neo4j or execute queries.

airtable-mcp.name: Airtable MCP Server
airtable-mcp.description: Provides scoped Airtable record and schema tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Use a current Node LTS runtime for SDK dependencies. Configure an Airtable personal access token, allowed bases/scopes, tool permissions and MCP client separately. Enabled tools can modify records or schemas; installation does not access Airtable or start the server.

mcp-for-blender.name: MCP for Blender
mcp-for-blender.description: Connects agents to Blender scene inspection and scripted content creation

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and Blender 3.0+ with its addon installed, enabled and connected separately. The current package/repository are mcp-for-blender, renamed from blender-mcp. Setup commands can edit client configuration and addon files; run them explicitly. Minimal anonymous usage telemetry is enabled by default; content collection needs opt-in. Set DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true to disable all telemetry. Tool execution can run Python in Blender.

browser-tools-mcp.name: BrowserTools MCP
browser-tools-mcp.description: Streams browser diagnostics and Lighthouse audits into coding-agent context

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22.19+ and Chrome with the upstream DevTools extension. The current 2.x server includes its connector; no separate connector server is required. Load the extension and configure the MCP client explicitly. Opening DevTools begins capture of the inspected session, which can contain application content. Installation does not install the extension or start capture.

swe-rex.name: SWE-ReX Remote Runtime
swe-rex.description: Serves interactive shell execution environments for coding agents

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. This entry exposes the swe-rex remote runtime CLI, swerex-remote, rather than a coding agent. The catalog targets macOS/Linux POSIX shell environments; Windows users can run inside WSL. Configure runtime isolation, access and any Docker/cloud backend explicitly. Optional provider extras are separate; installation does not start a command service.

opik.name: Opik CLI
opik.description: Configures agent tracing, evaluation and Opik service integrations

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The opik distribution includes its CLI; configure a chosen self-hosted endpoint or Comet credentials/workspace separately. Instrumentation, model-backed evaluation and MCP client registration are explicit steps. Installing the CLI does not deploy the Opik backend or upload application traces.

litserve.name: LitServe CLI
litserve.description: Builds and serves custom inference and agent pipeline APIs

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The litserve package supplies litserve and also a lightning executable; check alias conflicts. Define service code and install model/framework dependencies in its selected environment separately. Model downloads, GPU setup, service startup and cloud deployment are explicit operations.

prefect.name: Prefect CLI
prefect.description: Orchestrates and observes scheduled agent workflows and task execution

metadata.notes: The published package supports Python 3.10 through 3.14; current upstream development requires Python 3.11+. Configure a self-hosted API or cloud account, storage, work pools and deployment credentials separately. Optional integration packages are separate. Starting workers, running flows and deploying infrastructure are explicit operations.

open-webui.name: Open WebUI CLI
open-webui.description: Serves a self-hosted interface for model conversations and agent tool workflows

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.11 or 3.12; set UV_PYTHON=3.12 when installing to select a compatible interpreter. The Python open-webui distribution supplies the server CLI, distinct from the source frontend npm workspace. Native dependencies can impose OS/architecture limits. Configure authentication, storage, providers and tools separately. Service startup and any first-use embedding/model downloads are explicit steps.

resend-mcp.name: Resend MCP Server
resend-mcp.description: Provides configured email and Resend account tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22+. Uses the current resend-mcp package from resend/resend-mcp. Configure a Resend API key, verified sender/domain, account scopes, enabled tools and MCP client separately. Enabled operations can send email or modify account resources; installation does not authenticate, send messages or start the server.

contextforge.name: IBM ContextForge Gateway
contextforge.description: Federates agent MCP tools through a configurable gateway and administration service

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.12 or 3.13. This catalog method targets macOS/Linux; Windows users can run inside WSL. The base package supplies mcpgateway plus cforge, mcpplugins, init-secrets and mcpgateway-server aliases. Configure generated secrets, authentication, storage and upstream tool access before service startup. Optional plugins/backends need separate dependencies; installation does not start or expose a gateway.

jupyter-mcp.name: Jupyter MCP Server
jupyter-mcp.description: Gives agents configured notebook editing and kernel execution tools

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible native dependencies. The normalized jupyter-mcp-server distribution also supplies jupyter-mcp. Configure the notebook server, authentication/token, collaborative notebook extensions and MCP client separately. Optional sandbox providers need their own extras/credentials. Enabled tools can execute notebook code; installation does not start kernels or provision a sandbox.

logfire.name: Pydantic Logfire CLI
logfire.description: Configures tracing and observability for agent and language-model applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. Install logfire for its CLI; logfire-sdk alone does not supply this command. Authenticate and select a project/endpoint, then instrument the application explicitly. Framework-specific integrations can need optional extras. Traces may contain application/model content sent to the configured destination; installation does not add instrumentation or submit traces.

mlflow.name: MLflow CLI
mlflow.description: Tracks, evaluates and serves models and agent applications through MLflow

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible scientific/native dependencies. This method installs the base mlflow distribution and its CLI; MCP, GenAI gateway and provider-specific extras are separate. Configure tracking/artifact storage, authentication, model providers and serving environments explicitly. Installation does not start a server, run evaluations or deploy models.

harbor.name: Harbor Agent Evaluation CLI
harbor.description: Runs agent benchmarks and evaluation environments for coding-agent comparison

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.12+. This is harbor-framework/harbor from the Terminal-Bench creators, not the container registry project; the package also installs hb and hr aliases. The catalog targets macOS/Linux; Windows users can run inside WSL. Select datasets, agents, model credentials and Docker or a supported cloud environment explicitly. Runs can consume compute/provider credits; installation does not launch benchmarks or provision environments.

wandb.name: Weights and Biases CLI
wandb.description: Tracks agent experiments, evaluation runs and model artifacts

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible platform wheels. The wandb distribution supplies wandb and the wb alias. Configure login or offline mode, project scope and artifact destinations separately. Application instrumentation, sweeps and synchronization are explicit operations; selected runs/artifacts can be uploaded to the configured service. Installation does not start experiments or upload data.

modal.name: Modal CLI
modal.description: Runs and deploys agent functions and sandbox workloads on Modal

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.15 and compatible platform dependencies. The modal distribution includes its CLI. Configure authentication, project/environment scope, secrets and workload code explicitly. Agent skills installation, sandbox creation, remote execution and deployment are separate operations that can consume account resources.

vastai.name: Vast.ai CLI
vastai.description: Manages GPU instances and serverless compute for agent model workloads

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The canonical upstream is vast-ai/vast-cli and the published package is vastai; it also installs serve-vast-deployment. Configure API credentials, instance selection, storage and workload images separately. Renting instances, serverless deployment, data transfers and billing actions are explicit operations; installation provisions nothing.

gpustack.name: GPUStack CLI
gpustack.description: Serves and manages model inference infrastructure used by agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.12; select UV_PYTHON=3.12 when installing. This method targets Linux, matching current worker support; Windows workers require WSL2 and macOS workers are unsupported upstream. Configure Docker, suitable GPU drivers/container toolkit, server storage/authentication, workers and model backends separately. Installation does not start the service or download models.

ramalama.name: RamaLama CLI
ramalama.description: Runs and serves local model backends for agent workflows

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew formula, which manages Python and installs llama.cpp on macOS. Current bottles cover Apple silicon macOS and x64/arm64 Linux; other supported hosts may require source builds. Configure the chosen native or Podman/Docker runtime separately. Model pulls, container setup and inference/server startup are explicit operations.

zenml.name: ZenML CLI
zenml.description: Builds and deploys reproducible model and agent application pipelines

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. The base zenml package supplies its CLI; integrations and pipeline-specific dependencies are separate. Initialize a chosen repository and configure server authentication, artifact stores, stacks and deployment credentials explicitly. Installing the CLI does not create a stack, run a pipeline or provision infrastructure.

dstack.name: dstack CLI
dstack.description: Schedules model development and inference workloads on configured compute

metadata.notes: Uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew formula, including its managed Python environment and provider integrations. Current bottles cover Apple silicon macOS and x64/arm64 Linux; other supported hosts may need source builds. Configure or connect to a dstack server, project, backend credentials and workload files separately. Runs, fleets and deployments can allocate billable compute; installation does not start them.

promptflow.name: PromptFlow CLI
promptflow.description: Builds, runs and evaluates prompt and tool workflows for agent applications

metadata.notes: The published package supports Python 3.9+; use Python 3.12 for current dependencies. Promptflow is a metapackage: expose its promptflow-devkit dependency executable with uv with_executables_from while retaining promptflow for inventory, upgrades and removal. Older AgentManager binaries need the ENGIN-4 uv metadata support. Configure flow dependencies, provider connections and optional promptflow-tools/Azure integrations separately; installation does not run a flow.

deepcode.name: DeepCode CLI
deepcode.description: Runs durable coding-agent sessions through DeepCode terminal and local service tools

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.12+. Use deepcode-hku from HKUDS/DeepCode, which supplies deepcode and deepcode-app-server. Initialize storage and configure model providers, project trust and optional clients explicitly. Starting a client can launch its persistent local service; accepted work can continue after the client closes. Package installation does not initialize a project or start agent work.

codeflash.name: Codeflash CLI
codeflash.description: Optimizes Python code with agent-generated changes and benchmark verification

metadata.notes: The published package declares Python 3.9+; use a current compatible Python runtime. Configure Codeflash authentication, project paths, tests and benchmark environment separately. Optimization commands can generate tests, edit code, run subprocesses and submit selected code to the configured service; installation does not initialize or optimize a repository.

aws-agentcore.name: AWS AgentCore CLI
aws-agentcore.description: Scaffolds, observes and deploys agent applications on AWS AgentCore

metadata.notes: Requires Node 20+; use a current Node LTS runtime. This is the official @aws/agentcore CLI, distinct from the older Python starter toolkit. Its postinstall detects older toolkit installations and can warn about conflicts. Configure AWS credentials/region, permissions and project-specific Python, uv or deployment dependencies separately. Installation does not migrate a project or deploy AWS resources.

mcpc.name: Apify MCP Client
mcpc.description: Inspects and invokes MCP tools through a scriptable terminal client

metadata.notes: Requires Node 22.12+. Use @apify/mcpc from apify/mcpc, renamed from the mcp-cli repository; it supplies mcpc and mcpc-bridge. Configure server endpoints, transport and authentication explicitly. Connections can start selected stdio server commands and tool calls can modify connected services. Installation does not connect, authenticate or invoke tools.

bmad-method.name: BMad Method CLI
bmad-method.description: Installs structured agent skills and software delivery workflows into projects

metadata.notes: Uses the stable 6.12 npm release line, distinct from the upstream v7 preview branch. Requires Node 20.12+, Python 3.10+ and uv for workflow setup/scripts; use a current Node LTS runtime. The package supplies bmad and bmad-method. Run project installation and choose agent integrations explicitly; these commands write project skills/configuration. Installing the global wrapper does not configure a repository.

docling.name: Docling CLI
docling.description: Converts documents into structured context for agent retrieval and analysis

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible native/model dependencies. The published docling metapackage exposes docling and docling-tools itself and installs docling-slim with standard conversion features; no dependency-executable override is needed. Choose document inputs, OCR/model backends and optional formats explicitly. First use can download model weights; installation does not convert documents.

docling-serve.name: Docling Serve CLI
docling-serve.description: Serves document conversion APIs for agent ingestion and retrieval pipelines

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible Docling/native model dependencies. This installs the Python service CLI, separate from Docling container images. Configure bind address, authentication, storage, conversion backends and any UI options before starting it. First conversion may download model weights; installation does not expose a service or process documents.

docling-mcp.name: Docling MCP Server
docling-mcp.description: Provides document conversion and structured document tools to agent MCP clients

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+ and compatible native/model dependencies. The package is docling-mcp and its executable is docling-mcp-server. Choose local conversion or a configured remote Docling service, allowed inputs, optional retrieval/embedding backends and MCP client explicitly. Model downloads and server startup are separate steps; installation does not read or convert documents.

agentstack.name: Agent Stack CLI
agentstack.description: Installs and manages a local platform for deploying agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.14; set UV_PYTHON=3.14 to select it. Use agentstack-cli from i-am-bee/agentstack, not the unrelated agentstack PyPI package. The CLI also supplies agentstack-cli. Run agentstack self install separately to set up its Lima VM/Kubernetes platform; Linux needs QEMU. Windows needs WSL2 but the CLI must run natively in PowerShell, not inside WSL. Installation alone does not create the VM or deploy agents.

cognee.name: Cognee CLI
cognee.description: Builds and queries knowledge and graph memory for agent applications

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10 through 3.14 and compatible storage/embedding dependencies. The base cognee package supplies cognee-cli; select storage, datasets, embedding/model providers and credentials explicitly. Ingestion, graph construction and model downloads are separate operations. The optional UI needs Node/npm and its MCP service needs Docker; installing the CLI does not start them.

runpodctl.name: RunPod CLI
runpodctl.description: Manages GPU pods and serverless endpoints for agent model workloads

metadata.notes: Uses the official runpod/runpodctl Homebrew tap with universal macOS and x64/arm64 Linux release binaries. Configure API credentials, project scope, workload images and storage explicitly. Resource creation, endpoint invocation and transfers can consume account resources. The upstream CLI checks for updates during normal use; RUNPOD_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 disables that check. Installation does not provision workloads.

opensandbox-cli.name: OpenSandbox CLI
opensandbox-cli.description: Manages sandbox lifecycles and command execution for agent workloads

metadata.notes: Requires Python 3.10+. The opensandbox-cli distribution supplies osb and opensandbox, separate from opensandbox-server and the SDK package. Configure an existing OpenSandbox server endpoint, API key and runtime/egress policy explicitly; server deployment needs its own Docker/Kubernetes environment. Installation does not start a server, create a sandbox or execute commands.

trigger-dev.name: Trigger.dev CLI
trigger-dev.description: Develops and deploys background tasks and durable agent workflows

metadata.notes: The published wrapper declares Node 18.20+, but its posthog-node dependency requires Node 20.20+ on 20.x or 22.22+; use a current Node LTS runtime. The package trigger.dev supplies trigger. Configure project tasks, provider secrets and cloud/self-hosted access separately. Development workers and deployments can run tasks or allocate resources. Set TRIGGER_TELEMETRY_DISABLED to disable upstream telemetry; installation does not initialize or deploy a project.
